question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer implements SPAN configuration on a Nexus 5000 series switch. Which two commands are necessary to complete the SPAN session configuration? (Choose two.)
context:
N5K-Core(config)# monitor session 1 type fc
N5K-Core(config-monitor)# source interface fc2/1 rx
N5K-Core(config-monitor)# destination interface fc2/2
N5K-Core(config-monitor)# no shut
options: Configure switchport speed 4000 under interface fc2/2.
Configure the switchport monitor under interface fc2/2.
Configure session type fc under monitor session 1.
Configure the switchport mode SD under interface fc2/1.
Configure the switchport mode SD under interface fc2/2.
theory: A SPAN session on a Cisco Nexus/MDS switch needs both a defined session (source and destination interfaces, direction) and the destination interface must actually be placed in SD (SPAN Destination) port mode - simply naming it as a destination under the span session isn't enough. In this Fibre Channel SPAN scenario, interface fc2/2 must have 'switchport mode SD' configured and, because SD ports support only fixed lower speeds (no auto-negotiation), its speed must also be explicitly set to match, which is why both the switchport mode SD and switchport speed commands are required to complete the session. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 11 - SPAN)
